title: The Paper Uniform
premise: In the winter of 1899, widowed lighthouse keeper Ansel Sandoval lives quietly on a river bend, keeping the lamp lit and his past buried. When census taker Miriam Voss arrives and asks about a name that shouldn't exist in his ledger, she uncovers the truth: Ansel has been sheltering Elias Brandt, an old friend now declared an enemy of the state, honoring a promise made before the war split them apart. As the great storms batter the coast and suspicion closes in, Ansel, Miriam, and Elias must decide whether loyalty to a person outweighs loyalty to law. The novel ends as the ice breaks on the river: Elias escapes downstream under cover of the last storm, Miriam falsifies her final record at terrible cost to her career, and Ansel remains—no longer invisible, but no longer alone in knowing what justice sometimes requires.
about_author: Hazel Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs and census ledgers from coastal towns. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of official history.

chapters.title: The Lamp and the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet him mid-routine: trimming wicks, logging weather, eating alone in the keeper's cottage two years after his wife's death. The chapter establishes his creed—that history happens elsewhere—and ends with the first snow of the great storm year falling on the river.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. The census taker arrives by ferry, brisk and thorough. Her questions are routine until she notices a second set of boots by the door and a name scratched from the household list. She leaves without pressing—but writes the anomaly in her field notes.

chapters.title: The Man Below the Stairs
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, flashback woven into present. We learn who Elias Brandt is: a friend since boyhood, once a witness to Ansel's wedding, now hiding in the cellar because his name appears on a list of collaborators. The promise made in peacetime is revealed over cards and candlelight.

chapters.title: What the River Brings
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. Returning to verify her count, Miriam finds a rowboat half-sunk near the light—a boat that matches one reported stolen downstream. She says nothing to the harbormaster but begins, against her own instincts, to investigate privately.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The first great storm hits; the lamp must be kept burning through hurricane winds while Elias helps haul oil up ninety stairs. In shared labor, old intimacy returns, and Ansel admits how much he has missed being known.

chapters.title: The Field Notes
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. Back in town, Miriam cross-references her notes and discovers Elias was declared enemy after testifying against a powerful shipping family. Justice, she realizes, may have been purchased rather than served. Her doubt becomes dangerous curiosity.

chapters.title: A Visitor with Official Eyes
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A government inspector arrives unannounced, following the same paper trail Miriam left behind. Ansel lies smoothly for the first time in his life and hates how easily it comes. That night he tells Elias he may need to move on before the ice breaks.

chapters.title: The Widow's Coat
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. Miriam visits Ansel openly, returning a mended coat he lent her during the storm—an excuse. Their conversation circles each other, each recognizing the other knows more than they admit. A wary alliance begins to form beneath the politeness.

chapters.title: Peacetime Promises
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, first time. Through his eyes we see the cellar world: dust, memory, guilt. He recounts the promise—he once saved Ansel's life, and Ansel swore no war would make him a stranger. Elias fears the debt has become a chain dragging Ansel down with him.

chapters.title: Ice Lock
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The river freezes solid; escape by water is impossible until spring. The inspector returns with a warrant for 'a man matching no description,' and Ansel realizes someone local informed. Suspicion falls on the ferryman, but Ansel isn't sure.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Debt
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. Miriam traces the informant to the ferryman, who owes money to the shipping family. She confronts him quietly and buys his silence with her own savings—an act that compromises her neutrality and binds her fate to Ansel's.

chapters.title: Three at Table
chapters.summary: Rotating POV across one dinner scene. For the first time all three share a room above the cellar. Conversation is coded, tender, and tense; Miriam sees Elias's face for the first time and must decide what she has seen. The chapter ends with a toast to 'absent friends.'

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. In the county archive, Miriam finds the original testimony that condemned Elias—and evidence it was coerced. She copies it, knowing forgery or theft of records means prison. Her loyalty shifts fully from institution to truth.

chapters.title: The Second Storm
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The worst storm of the year strikes; a ship founders on the shoal and Ansel, exhausted, misjudges the lamp's timing. Survivors reach shore, including a crewman who recognizes Elias's silhouette in the tower window.

chapters.title: Seen
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The crewman says nothing immediately, but Elias knows the arithmetic of fear. He prepares to surrender himself to save Ansel, writing a confession letter. Ansel finds it and burns it, refusing to let the promise end this way.

chapters.title: The Inspector's Patience
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. The inspector, no fool, sets a trap: a rumor that the warrant will be executed at week's end, hoping to flush the fugitive into motion. Miriam learns of it and must warn Ansel without revealing how she knows—or why she cares.

chapters.title: Breaking Point
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel confronts the crewman on the ice road and appeals not to mercy but to memory—the man's own brother was once hidden from the law. The crewman agrees to silence, but the encounter is witnessed from shore by the inspector's clerk.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. The clerk reports; the inspector moves up the timeline. Miriam faces her reckoning: submit her census book with the erased name exposed, or alter the official record itself. In a quiet, devastating scene, she dips her pen and commits her crime of mercy.

chapters.title: Before the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The plan is set: the third storm will mask a departure downriver in the ferryman's boat, timed to the ice break. Elias and Ansel climb the tower one last time; Elias lights the lamp himself, a small act of restored citizenship. They exchange the promise again, finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Last Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs in short sections. The climax: the escape runs alongside the storm's peak. The inspector waits at the ferry landing but Miriam misdirects him with a forged telegram; the boat slips past in whiteout. The ice groans, cracks, and gives way just as the boat clears the bend.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Ink
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. Consequences arrive: Miriam is dismissed for irregularities but spared prosecution when the altered record conveniently cannot be proven hers. She leaves town by the same ferry, pausing at the light. Ansel watches her go, understanding that her sacrifice bought his friend's life and cost her everything else.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Log
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, epilogue. Spring. Ansel writes the season's first log entry and, for the first time, records something true beyond weather: a line acknowledging the man who sheltered below, the woman who rewrote the books, and the promise kept. History, he finally understands, happened here—to him—and he chose his part in it.
